candidates.source_name: CEJN — Crnogorski elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (Portal javne nabavke), Tenders section
candidates.why_relevant: Mandatory national e-procurement system for all Montenegrin budget entities; every tender notice, tendering documentation, award decision and concluded contract for banking, payment, card, ATM and core-banking services must pass through it. Contract award records name vendor, value and dates that no vendor press release discloses.
candidates.access_status: public listing; full functionality and some documents may require registered account
candidates.legal_status: official government publication, public by law (Zakon o javnim nabavkama)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the tenders listing with keyword/CPV filters (bankarske usluge, platni promet, POS, kartice, bankomat, core banking); persist notice IDs and diff for new award notices. Fall back to headless browser if the listing is JS-rendered — a plain fetch returned an empty shell in this run.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the national procurement portal, then snowball from the Directorate for Public Procurement Policy
queries_used: portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora CEJN elektronske javne nabavke
javna nabavka bankarske usluge Crna Gora obavještenje o dodjeli ugovora
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch of https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned essentially no page content — hypothesis: client-side rendered listing, not a dead page. Unverified.

candidates.source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki, Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (former Uprava za javne nabavke / UJN)
candidates.why_relevant: Policy and methodology owner for Montenegrin public procurement: publishes the Law, bylaws (pravilnici), standard notice forms (Obrazac 18 etc.), annual reports on the procurement system, registration instructions for CEJN, and an 'EU tenderi' category. Best single pointer for understanding notice structure, field semantics and where each document type is published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the bylaws and standard-forms pages once to build a field dictionary for notice parsing; subscribe to the news and 'EU tenderi' categories for changes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball from CEJN query

candidates.source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki — Rješenja (procurement review body decisions)
candidates.why_relevant: Appeal decisions in procurement disputes. These name the contracting authority, the complaining and winning bidders, the technical specification at issue and the price — often disclosing competitive detail (who bid, on what terms) that never appears in the award notice alone. High signal for contested banking/POS/ATM tenders.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the rjesenja register, keyword-filter decision text for bank/payment vendor and service terms, extract parties and subject matter.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the procurement review commission; corrected the guessed domain (kzp.gov.me) to the actual one

negative_findings.description: Fetch of https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned no usable page content — no listing rows, no filters, no URLs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hypothesis: the tender listing is client-side rendered or bot-defended, not dead. The domain is repeatedly cited as the live official portal by ujn.gov.me, gov.me and multiple aggregators, so it is recorded as unverified-but-almost-certainly-live, never as dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell may need a headless browser or an internal JSON/API endpoint rather than a plain HTTP fetch; the collection design must budget for that.

negative_findings.description: Targeted local-language searches for concrete Montenegrin banking/payment procurement items ('POS terminal', 'platne kartice', 'bankarske usluge', 'bankomat') returned portal home pages and Bosnian/Serbian equivalents rather than actual ME notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: No individual Montenegrin banking-services or POS/card tender document was located through open web search in this run. The closest hits were a BiH treasury banking-services tender and BiH award notices on ejn.gov.ba — different jurisdiction, not usable for ME.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Montenegrin notice text appears to be poorly indexed by general search engines (consistent with a JS-rendered portal). Item-level discovery will have to happen inside CEJN's own search, not via web search — a structural constraint on this workstream.

negative_findings.description: The procurement review commission does not live at the plausible-looking kzp.gov.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Its decisions register is at kontrola-nabavki.me/rjesenja (admin instance at admin.kontrola-nabavki.me); contact email komisija@nabavka.gov.me. The guessed gov.me subdomain was not found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Illustrates that ME procurement institutions are scattered across gov.me, .me and .co.me domains; any seed list built by pattern-guessing gov.me subdomains will silently miss sources.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific banking or payment-services notice was retrievable from TED via general web search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only TED's own explanatory pages and one EU Delegation security-services tender surfaced. Whether ME entities publish to TED at all (Montenegro is a candidate country, not an EU member) was not established in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: TED's value for this cell may be limited to EU-Delegation/IPA contracts rather than national ME procurement; the collection plan should test this before investing in TED tooling.

negative_findings.description: The World Bank project id for the Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA (TIPS clone) operation was not confirmed against a project page.
negative_findings.result_summary: A 2025 disclosure PDF filename contains 'P509405', which is suggestive but not verified as this project's id. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a fact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The project id is the join key to the procurement plan and award data on Finances One; getting it wrong would silently pull the wrong pipeline.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed machine-readable access path (API, bulk export, RSS, or stable notice-URL pattern) into CEJN, the mandatory national portal.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a headless-browser session against cejn.gov.me/tenders, capture the XHR calls behind the listing, and document the real query endpoint and notice-URL pattern; check whether CEJN exposes an OCDS (Open Contracting Data Standard) feed, which the EU-funded design makes plausible.

coverage_gaps.description: Only CBCG and Pošta Crne Gore were pinned down as individual contracting authorities. The rest of the payment-relevant buyer set is unenumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an actor map of ME contracting authorities that buy banking/payment services: Ministarstvo finansija / Državni trezor, Uprava prihoda i carina, Uprava za katastar, EPCG, Crnogorski elektroprenosni sistem, Vodovod/Komunalne usluge companies, Fond PIO, Fond zdravstva, Univerzitet CG, and the 25 opštine — then locate each one's 'javne nabavke' page and CEJN buyer id.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV-code mapping was established for the ME/banking-payments intersection, and no glossary of the noisy terms was validated against real notice text.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fix a CPV filter set (66100000 banking, 66110000, 66172000 payment transaction processing, 30123000/302xx terminals, 48/72 series banking software and IT services) and a sr keyword list (bankarske usluge, platni promet, POS terminal, bankomat, kartično poslovanje, procesiranje transakcija, jezgro bankarskog sistema, elektronsko bankarstvo). Flag 'nabavka', 'usluga' and 'kartice' as high-noise on their own.

coverage_gaps.description: Unknown how far back CEJN's public archive reaches and whether pre-2019 notices from the old UJN portal (ujn.gov.me / portal.ujn.gov.me) remain retrievable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe CEJN's earliest published notice date; check the Internet Archive for the legacy UJN portal to recover the pre-CEJN award history needed for multi-year vendor-share analysis.

coverage_gaps.description: Low-value 'jednostavne nabavke' (simple procurements, governed by a separate pravilnik) and direct negotiated awards may sit outside the main notice stream.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read the Pravilnik o načinu sprovođenja jednostavnih nabavki on ujn.gov.me to establish where and whether such awards are published; if they are only on buyers' own sites, that raises the priority of per-institution scraping.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI-financed procurement executed by ME clients is split across ECEPP, World Bank STEP/Finances One, and the national portal, with no confirmed way to join records across them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For the TIPS/SEPA and fiscal-stability operations, retrieve the procurement plan and map each planned package to its publication channel, so a single vendor-award timeline can be assembled.

brief: Montenegro's public-procurement route to banking and payments intelligence is anchored on one mandatory national system, CEJN (cejn.gov.me), which by law carries every stage from plan to concluded contract for all budget entities — but it did not yield content to a plain fetch in this run, so item-level discovery will likely require a headless browser or its underlying API rather than web search, which surfaced no individual Montenegrin banking or POS tender at all. Around that core sit high-value satellites: the procurement review commission's decision register at kontrola-nabavki.me (naming bidders and disputed specifications), DRI audit reports that itemise treasury banking and payment costs, and the buyer pages of CBCG and Pošta Crne Gore, the two institutions whose purchases are most reliably payment-relevant. The IFI layer is currently the richest forward pipeline: the World Bank's EUR 8m Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA 'TIPS clone' operation implies a multi-year sequence of instant-payment procurement packages published across Finances One and STEP, while EBRD notices moved wholesale to ECEPP and EBRD project disclosures name the Montenegrin counterparty banks (NLB Podgorica, CKB, Alter Modus) whose expansion precedes technology buying. Commercial aggregators (nabavke.com, javne-nabavke.com, eKapija) are useful redundancy and provide market denominators, but are paywalled and must be verified against the CEJN original before anything is treated as fact.
